exposure: interpregnancy body mass index (BMI) change (> 1 unit, < -1 unit, -1 to 1 unit)
cohort: The study analyzed data from 2,861 Japanese women in their first and second pregnancies who delivered singletons between 2000 and 2022.
finding: Interpregnancy weight gain was associated with an increased risk of gestational diabetes mellitus and delivering a large-for-gestational-age neonate, while weight loss was linked to a decreased risk of gestational diabetes mellitus.
gest_age: preterm birth, large for gestational age neonate
